overview: Black takes the centre with ...d5 and ...c5 against White's 1.g3 fianchetto. White follows with Nf3, O-O and d3 or c4, and the game usually reaches a flexible, reversed Sicilian or English structure where White plays on the long diagonal and Black has space. Little theory, long manoeuvring.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto, castle and pressure d5 and the long diagonal.
Play c4 or d3 and e4 depending on Black's set-up.

black_ideas.idea: Develop and fianchetto to meet White's flank play.

typical_structures.structure: Black c5/d5 against a White g2 bishop; flexible English or reversed-Sicilian shapes.

character.notes: Slow manoeuvring with no forcing tactics.

structure.notes: Flank opening with the centre undecided.

approach.notes: White's 1.g3 set-up is playable against nearly anything.

level.notes: Minimal theory, but slow plans take feel.

character.reason: Neither especially forcing nor especially hard to crack.

structure.reason: Flank opening with the centre not yet decided.

approach.reason: White's 1.g3 and Bg2 set-up works against many replies.

plans.reason: The long diagonal bishop is the core idea.
